text.title: Multi-Agent Design Patterns — Core Rules
text.summary: Ten testable rules that gate any application of the multi-agent-design-patterns methodology — r1-r5 govern how the mesh is operated (tiering, handoff contracts, termination, tracing), r1-one-named-pattern..r5-hitl-on-irreversible govern which topology is selected and how the choice is recorded. Sources: Anthropic — Building Effective Agents (engineering blog 2024); OpenAI Agents SDK documentation; LangGraph multi-agent patterns.

rule.statement: Pick the multi-agent pattern based on task decomposability: orchestrator-worker for parallelisable subtasks, hierarchical for tree-shaped projects, sequential for pipeline tasks, debate for consensus problems.
rule.rationale: Mis-picked patterns make the system harder to debug than a single-agent baseline; the decomposition shape is the load-bearing signal.

rule.statement: Use a model ladder: orchestrator = Claude Opus / GPT-4o, workers = Sonnet / GPT-4o-mini, classifiers = Haiku / GPT-3.5; never run the entire mesh on the most expensive model.
rule.rationale: Naive uniform-Opus deployments cost 5–20× more than tiered ones with no measurable quality lift.

rule.statement: Define an explicit handoff contract per agent edge: input schema, output schema, error-channel, max-turns; never implicit-pass-through arbitrary chat history.
rule.rationale: Implicit context-passing causes silent context drift and is the #1 cause of multi-agent quality regressions.

rule.statement: Wire a global termination condition (max steps OR cumulative cost OR done-tool fired) that overrides any individual agent's loop.
rule.rationale: Without a global cap, a single mis-routed handoff can run a workflow into the ground; emergency shutdown must be explicit, not emergent.

rule.statement: Emit a tracing span for every agent invocation and every cross-agent edge (input, output, latency, cost, model id); store traces for replay.
rule.rationale: Multi-agent regressions are unreproducible without traces; the replay capability is what distinguishes a system from a demo.

rule.statement: A multi-agent system MUST declare exactly ONE primary pattern from the 8-canonical set in its design.md. Stacking ("Hierarchical + Loop + HITL") is forbidden; nest patterns explicitly (e.g. Hierarchical contains a Loop sub-graph for one worker).
rule.rationale: One named pattern keeps the decision auditable. Stacks hide the actual shape and make pattern-specific failure modes invisible to reviewers.

rule.statement: The decision record MUST link to the downstream impl methodology: Sequential / Parallel → `multi-agent-basics`; Hierarchical → `multi-agent-hierarchical`; Generator-Critic / Loop → `multi-agent-conversational`; Blackboard → `multi-agent-collaborative`; Router / HITL → `multi-agent-production-bus`.
rule.rationale: Without a downstream link the decision is academic; implementations drift from intent.

rule.statement: Blackboard pattern selection REQUIRES an explicit concurrency-control plan (single-writer queue, CRDT, or DB transactions). Without it the choice is silently incorrect.
rule.rationale: Blackboard means agents share mutable state; concurrent writes without coordination produce non-deterministic results.

rule.statement: Router pattern selection REQUIRES a documented classifier with measured accuracy (≥0.85 on a held-out test set) or a deterministic rule set. A router that hand-waves the routing decision is just an orchestrator on cheap labels.
rule.rationale: Router pattern only pays off if the routing decision is cheap AND accurate; a fuzzy classifier degrades to broadcast or worse.

rule.statement: Every irreversible action in the design (DB writes, payments, external emails, deploys) MUST be gated by Human-in-the-Loop OR a typed approval check. Selecting any other primary pattern does NOT exempt the design from this gate.
rule.rationale: Irreversible actions on autopilot are the dominant production failure mode for any multi-agent system regardless of pattern.
